findings.reason: the case must name a measure the matcher reads ("run the test suite", "pytest tests/…"), or the node writes a positive assertion that cannot hold as worded.
findings.text: the sixth case requires a refusal for "an entry whose role the flight config declares execution_capable: false … and whose done-when needs execution", but `assess_execution_fit` (reckon/capability.py:102) refuses only when `_EXECUTION_MEASURE_PATTERNS` (capability.py:39–49) match, and those match only "run/runs/running … test(s)/test suite/suite" or "pytest …". A done-when that plainly "needs execution" — "run the lane", "execute the script", "the interpolator runs" — matches neither pattern, so the case stores instead of refusing and the control "omitting execution fit … stores the sixth case's entry" passes for the wrong reason.

findings.reason: the refusal reads `execution_capable`, which `_effective_backend` takes from the role overlay rather than the lane (routing.py:180–190 applies the role overlay first, and no lane block declares the key), so a rebound lane cannot change the verdict; only the sentence justifying the choice is imprecise, and no test or symbol changes.
findings.text: §2 justifies fixing execution fit at queue time by calling the lane `queue_requests` records "the lane the admission pass launches it on", but admission does move a queued request's backend: `_local_fallback` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py near line 647) rewrites the pointer's `backend` to `local_backend` on a hold, and `_record_queued_on` (near line 1242) stamps a different lane when a route is moved. The written guarantee is therefore not one the code gives.
